solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Childless person is neither a ….? It's a prospect

parts.note: a person with no children cannot be called pa, the familiar word for father
neither pairs with nor, the word the sentence needs next
the blank is the other parent a childless person cannot be: ma, for mother

explanation.surface: A riddle about a childless person, with the blank filled in turning out to be a view.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap: a childless person is neither a PA NOR A MA (father, mother). Run together, those words spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide view over a landscape is a prospect, the sense of an outlook or vista.

clue.text: Advancement holds benefit for youngster

indicators.note: one word holding another means the second sits inside the first

parts.note: an advancement or rise is an ascent
the dole is state benefit paid to the unemployed in Britain

explanation.surface: Promotion that comes with a payout for a young worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The DOLE is British slang for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a youngster, someone in the stage between child and adult.

clue.text: Horse's saddle disintegrated in cold alkaline solution

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed in the solution named next

parts.note: lye is an alkaline solution used in soap-making

indicators.note: something that has disintegrated has fallen apart, so the letters of saddle are rearranged

explanation.surface: A horse's saddle rotting away after being dropped into a caustic bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disintegrated' rearranges the letters of the saddle; 'in' places them inside the alkaline solution. Lye is caustic soda or potash solution.
explanation.definitionFit: A Clydesdale is a heavy Scottish breed of draught horse.

clue.text: After reflection go out to lunch

indicators.note: a mirror reflection shows a word back to front, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to have a go is to have a stab at something

explanation.surface: Thinking things over before heading out for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out to lunch' looks like a plan for midday; it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal terms for someone crazy or not quite all there.

clue.text: Buff needs November off, and March?

indicators.note: with a letter off, it is removed from the word

parts.note: a buff or expert is a demon, as in a demon at chess
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An enthusiast who needs time off in both November and March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month after November; the question mark flags it as a protest march.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest march is a demonstration, shortened in everyday speech.

clue.text: Song is live on the radio

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is only heard, so it signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: to live a life is to lead it

explanation.surface: A singer's track is being broadcast live.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAD (as in lead a quiet life) sounds like LIED, said 'leed'. 'live' looks like an adjective about the broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lied is a German art song, such as those by Schubert.

clue.text: Frank perhaps is turning a brownish colour

indicators.note: turning a word round means reading its letters backwards

parts.note: Anne Frank is an example of someone surnamed Frank

explanation.surface: Someone called Frank changing colour, going brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like the first name of someone like Sinatra; it is the diarist Anne Frank's surname. 'turning' reverses ANNE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment, a yellowish or reddish brown.

clue.text: Solo perhaps by key composer

parts.note: Han Solo is a Star Wars character, so Han is an example of a Solo
Del is the delete key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A solo piece written in a certain key by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solo' and 'key' look musical; Solo is Han Solo and the key is the computer's delete key.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was the German-born Baroque composer of Messiah.

clue.text: Drink and a saucy sandwich I provided

indicators.note: to sandwich something is to hold it between two layers, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: saucy, meaning cheeky, is pert
provided, as in on condition that, means if

explanation.surface: Ordering a drink and a cheeky sandwich, if someone else supplies them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwich' looks like food on the menu; it puts I inside PERT.
explanation.definitionFit: An apéritif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Fathom what creates slick defeat

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for fathom, a unit of depth
a slick is a film of oil spilt on water

explanation.surface: Trying to work out what causes a slick of defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fathom' looks like a verb meaning understand; it is the unit of depth, F.
explanation.definitionFit: To foil a plan is to thwart or defeat it.

clue.text: Don't initially spend time struggling with One Down

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of the word is taken
struggling suggests things in disarray, and with joins the last word to the pool, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: spend is taken as written and time is shortened to its usual abbreviation T

explanation.surface: Advice not to spend time battling against a clue called One Down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes D from Don't; 'struggling' rearranges SPEND, T and ONE into ESPONDENT. 'One Down' looks like a crossword reference, but 'Down' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means feeling low or dejected, the same as being downcast.

clue.text: Deep sea fish

definitions.meaning: low in pitch, as a deep voice

explanation.surface: A fish from the deep ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, deep-sea fish, but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass voice is deep, and the bass is an edible sea fish.

clue.text: Jack's stockist picked up item of tableware

indicators.note: a sound picked up is heard, so this signals words that sound like others

parts.note: a jack or jack tar is a sailor, also called a salt; a stockist is someone who sells goods, a seller

explanation.surface: A sailor's supplier lifting a piece of crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and salt both mean a sailor; a seller of salt sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dish or shaker for salt set on a dining table is tableware.

clue.text: Look to employ contemptible sort

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, as in lo and behold
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: Planning to take on an unpleasant character.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a louse brands them a despicable, worthless person.

clue.text: Converse with heartless criminal involved in fraud

indicators.note: being involved in something puts one piece inside another

parts.note: a fraud or swindler is a cheat

indicators.note: with the heart gone, the central letter is removed

parts.note: a thief is a criminal

explanation.surface: Talking to a cold-blooded crook who is mixed up in a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle I of THIEF, giving THEF; W and THEF go 'involved in' CHEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To chew the fat is an idiom for chatting idly, to converse at leisure.

clue.text: Playing con moto grabs one after endless slow movement

indicators.note: one piece placed after another comes second in the answer
without its ends, only the middle of the word remains
grabbing something holds it inside
playing with letters rearranges them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A musician playing con moto (with motion) in a slow movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' gives LO from slow; 'Playing' rearranges CON MOTO into COMOTON, which 'grabs' I. 'con moto' and 'movement' look musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Locomotion is the act or power of moving from place to place.

clue.text: Mark gets unbeatable service in tennis club

parts.note: an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch

explanation.surface: A player named Mark hits an ace at the tennis club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tennis club' reads as one place, but 'club' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy club with a spiked or flanged head.

clue.text: Occupy the middle of Renault Clio?

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is taken

parts.note: Clio is the Muse of history in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Sitting in the centre of a Renault Clio car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Renault Clio' looks like the car; Clio is a Muse.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to keep them occupied or entertained.

clue.text: One who does plan, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a chart is a plan or map

explanation.surface: Someone who acts rather than just plans, most of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' is the British sense of cleaning: a char is a cleaner who 'does' for a household.
explanation.definitionFit: A char or charwoman is a cleaner, someone who does the housework.

clue.text: One gathering envelopes posted one's present? No

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: envelopes as a verb means wraps around, putting one piece inside another

parts.note: a bee is a gathering, as in a sewing bee
something posted has been sent

explanation.surface: Someone collecting envelopes posted as a gift, then refusing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'envelopes' looks like the noun beside 'posted'; it is the containment verb. The definition is a riddle: someone who isn't present.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is a person who is missing, the opposite of someone in attendance.

clue.text: Son takes lead perhaps, embracing extremely tight community

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside

parts.note: lead is an example of a chemical element

indicators.note: the extremes of the word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A boy taking a dog's lead and hugging a close-knit group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a dog lead; it is the metal. 'extremely' gives TT from tight.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement is a place where people live together, a village or colony.

clue.text: Blow out flame once fit

parts.note: an old flame is a former partner, an ex
hale means healthy and fit

explanation.surface: Extinguishing a flame that was once suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow out' and 'flame' suggest a candle; the flame is a former lover.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe out is to blow air out of the lungs.

clue.text: Failed in audition for film

indicators.note: audition is hearing, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: to have failed to hit is to have missed

explanation.surface: An actor flopped at the screen test for a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' and 'film' suggest acting; audition here means hearing. 'film' is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A film of moisture is a mist, a thin haze or coating.

clue.text: Penny-pinching, he takes a first sign of cost badly?

definitions.text: Penny-pinching, he takes a first sign of cost badly?

indicators.note: pinching something holds it tight inside
the first sign of a word is its opening letter
done badly means the letters come out disordered

explanation.surface: A miser who resents even the faintest hint of expense.
explanation.walkthrough: C from 'first sign of' cost, then 'badly' rearranges HE TAKES A, which, 'pinching' P, gives HEAPSKATE. The whole clue also describes a skinflint.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser who hates spending even a penny is a skinflint.

clue.text: Old sausage dog needs trimming

indicators.note: trimming cuts away letters at each end, leaving a run from inside the phrase

explanation.surface: An elderly dachshund overdue for a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: A sausage dog is a dachshund; 'trimming' it leaves the letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means elderly, having lived a long time.

clue.text: Capital city is area in decline

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: the sun sets when it declines

explanation.surface: A capital whose district is going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: The seat of government is the capital, the city where power is based.

clue.text: One runs a plant

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone managing a factory or plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory that someone runs; it is a living plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus of maples, so an acer is a tree.

clue.text: Smack little pest about

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a gnat is a small biting insect

explanation.surface: Swatting a small insect buzzing around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' looks like a slap; it means a taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack of something is a slight taste or flavour of it.

clue.text: Cut off a right mischief-maker

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Shunning a real troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a right' looks like an intensifier; it is A then a legal right.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate or estrange someone is to cut them off.

clue.text: Bird eggs brought back will get scrambled etc.

indicators.note: brought back means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ova are eggs, in Latin

indicators.note: scrambled letters are mixed up, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eggs returned to the kitchen to be scrambled, among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' and 'eggs' suggest breakfast. ETC rearranges to CET.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with an upturned bill.
